pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날에, 산골 마을에 순이라는 소녀가 살았어요. 순이네는 아주 가난해서 밥이 늘 한 그릇뿐이었지만, 순이는 마음이 참 고왔지요. 어느 저녁, 부뚜막 구석에서 무언가 꼬물꼬물— 손바닥만 한 두꺼비 한 마리가 순이를 빤히 올려다보았답니다.
pages.t: Long, long ago, in a village up in the mountains, there lived a girl named Suni. Suni's family was so poor that there was only ever one bowl of rice, but Suni had a truly kind heart. One evening, something wriggled in the corner of the kitchen stove ledge — a toad no bigger than her hand was looking right up at her.

pages.ko: 순이는 밥주걱으로 제 밥을 조금 덜어, 작은 종지에 소복이 담아 주었어요. "두껍아 두껍아, 한 술 먹어라! 쑥쑥 자라라, 한 술 더 먹어라!" 두꺼비는 오물오물 밥을 먹고는 배를 볼록 내밀었답니다.
pages.t: Suni took her rice paddle and scooped a little of her own rice into a tiny dish, heaped up nice and full. "Toady, toady, have a spoonful! Grow big and strong, have one more spoonful!" The toad munched up every bit and puffed out its round little tummy.

pages.ko: 그날부터 순이는 날마다 밥을 나누었어요. 봄이 가고, 여름이 가고, 잎이 노랗게 물들 무렵— 두꺼비는 무럭무럭 자라 어느새 강아지만큼 커졌지 뭐예요! 순이가 부르면 뒤뚱뒤뚱, 그림자처럼 졸졸 따라다녔답니다.
pages.t: From that day on, Suni shared her rice every single day. Spring went by, summer went by, and by the time the leaves turned yellow — the toad had grown and grown until it was as big as a puppy! Whenever Suni called, it came waddling after her like a shadow.

pages.ko: 밤이면 순이는 툇마루에 앉아 무명실로 해진 옷을 기웠어요. 두꺼비는 그 옆에 배를 척 붙이고 앉아 순이를 지켜보았지요. "두껍아 두껍아, 한 술 먹어라! 쑥쑥 자라라, 한 술 더 먹어라!" 순이가 흥얼거리면 두꺼비는 끔뻑끔뻑 눈을 감았다 떴어요.
pages.t: At night, Suni sat on the wooden porch and mended her worn clothes with white cotton thread. The toad settled down beside her, belly flat against the floor, and watched her. "Toady, toady, have a spoonful! Grow big and strong, have one more spoonful!" When Suni hummed it, the toad slowly blinked its eyes, open and shut, open and shut.

pages.ko: 그런데 이 마을에는 걱정거리가 하나 있었어요. 뒷산 낡은 사당에 아주 커다란 지네가 산다는 이야기였지요. 지네가 성을 내면 밤새 바람이 우웅우웅 울고 곡식이 시들시들해졌어요. 그래서 해마다 가을이면 마을에서 한 사람이 사당에 불을 밝히고 하룻밤을 지켜야 했답니다. 사당에 불이 꺼지면 지네가 마을로 내려온다고 했거든요.
pages.t: But this village had one big worry. People said an enormous centipede lived in the old shrine up on the hill behind them. When the centipede grew angry, the wind moaned oooo-oooo all night long, and the crops withered away. So every autumn, one person from the village had to light a lamp in the shrine and keep watch there for one whole night. For if the light in the shrine ever went out, they said, the centipede would come down into the village.

pages.ko: 올해는 순이네 차례였어요. 하지만 순이네에는 순이밖에 없었지요. 어른들은 어쩔 줄 몰라 서로 얼굴만 쳐다보았어요. 그때 순이가 조그맣게 손을 번쩍 들었답니다. "제가 갈게요." 아주 작은 목소리였지만, 아주 씩씩했어요. "안 될 말이다, 내가 가마." 할아버지가 지팡이를 짚고 일어섰어요. "할아버지, 산길은 제가 더 잘 올라요. 불만 밝히고 오면 되잖아요." 할아버지는 초롱에 불을 붙여 순이 손에 쥐여 주었어요. "그럼 산 밑에서 밤새 기다리마."
pages.t: This year it was Suni's family's turn. But there was nobody in Suni's house except Suni. The grown-ups did not know what to do and only looked at one another. Then Suni raised her small hand high. "I will go." It was a very small voice, but a very brave one. "That will never do. I shall go," said Grandfather, pushing himself up on his walking stick. "Grandfather, I climb the mountain path better than you do. I only have to light the lamp and come back, don't I?" So Grandfather lit the lantern and pressed it into Suni's hand. "Then I will wait all night at the foot of the mountain."

pages.ko: 해가 지자 순이는 할아버지가 밝혀 준 청사초롱을 꼭 쥐고 뒷산 길을 올랐어요. 발밑에서 낙엽이 바스락바스락. 순이는 몰랐지만, 저만치 뒤에서 두꺼비가 뒤뚱뒤뚱 조용히 따라오고 있었지요.
pages.t: When the sun went down, Suni held tight to the blue silk lantern Grandfather had lit for her and climbed the path up the hill. Under her feet the fallen leaves went crunch, crunch, crunch. Suni did not know it, but a little way behind her, the toad was waddling quietly along.

pages.ko: 낡은 사당 안은 캄캄하고 조용했어요. 순이는 청사초롱을 문고리 옆에 걸고 무릎을 꼭 끌어안았지요. 그때 창호지 문 위로 스르륵— 길고 커다란 그림자가 지나갔어요.
pages.t: Inside the old shrine it was dark and very, very still. Suni hung the blue silk lantern beside the door handle and hugged her knees up tight. Just then, something long and huge slid across the paper door — swoosh.

pages.ko: 삐거덕— 문이 스르르 열렸어요. 국수 가락처럼 흐물흐물한 다리가 하나, 둘, 셋… 문지방을 슬금슬금 넘어왔지요. "누구냐! 내 사당에 누가 왔느냐!" 우렁우렁 울리는 목소리에 순이는 눈을 꼭 감았답니다.
pages.t: Creeeak — the door swung slowly open. Legs as wobbly as noodles came sliding over the doorsill, one, two, three… "Who's there! Who has come into my shrine!" The voice boomed and rumbled, and Suni squeezed her eyes shut.

pages.ko: "두껍아… 두껍아…" 순이가 떨리는 목소리로 불렀어요. 그러자 툭— 순이 앞으로 두꺼비가 폴짝 뛰어나왔지요. 손바닥만 하던 그 두꺼비가, 산더미 같은 그림자 앞을 떡 하니 가로막고 버티고 섰답니다.
pages.t: "Toady… toady…" Suni called in a trembling voice. And then — thump! — the toad came hopping out in front of her. That toad, once no bigger than her hand, planted itself firmly in front of that mountain-sized shadow and would not budge one bit.

pages.ko: 두꺼비는 목을 크게 부풀리고 우엉— 우엉— 우렁차게 울었어요. 낡은 사당이 웅웅 울렸지요. 그러고는 발로 청사초롱을 슬쩍 밀어, 제 그림자를 벽에 산더미만큼 크게 비추었답니다. 사당 안이 캄캄해서, 지네 눈에는 커다란 그림자밖에 보이지 않았지요. "으앗! 나보다 큰 놈이잖아!"
pages.t: The toad puffed its throat up big and bellowed — woo-oomph! woo-oomph! The old shrine rang and hummed. Then it gave the blue silk lantern a little push with its foot, so that its own shadow spread up the wall as big as a mountain. It was so dark inside the shrine that all the centipede could see was that enormous shadow. "Yikes! He's even bigger than me!"

pages.ko: 지네는 놀라서 다리가 서로 엉켰어요. 우당탕탕! 문지방에 코를 콩 찧고는, 꽁지가 빠지게 산 너머로 달아났지요. "다시는, 다시는 안 올 테다!" 그 소리가 점점 멀어지더니 이내 조용해졌답니다.
pages.t: The centipede was so startled that all its legs got tangled together. Crash, bang, tumble! It bumped its nose on the doorsill and ran off over the mountain as fast as its legs could carry it. "Never, never again will I come back!" The sound grew fainter and fainter, and then all was quiet.

pages.ko: 그런데 두꺼비가 폭삭— 힘이 다 빠져 주저앉았어요. 순이는 두꺼비를 두 손으로 폭 안고 흔들었지요. "두껍아 두껍아, 한 술 먹어라! 쑥쑥 자라라, 어서 눈을 떠 봐!" 아침 해가 사당 문으로 스며들자, 두꺼비가 끔뻑— 눈을 떴답니다. 그날부터 마을은 다시 평화로워졌고, 순이와 두꺼비는 오래오래 함께 밥을 나누며 살았어요. 작은 마음으로 나눈 밥 한 술이 이렇게 큰 은혜로 돌아온대요.
pages.t: But then the toad flopped down, all its strength gone. Suni gathered it up in both arms and rocked it. "Toady, toady, have a spoonful! Grow big and strong — please open your eyes!" And when the morning sun came shining in through the shrine door, the toad blinked its eyes open. From that day on the village was peaceful again, and Suni and the toad shared their rice together for a long, long time. One little spoonful, shared with a kind heart, can come back to you as a great, great kindness.
